content.text:
I'm mapping out the grid nodes and computing edge weights between them along rows and columns, building the distance structure for the graph.

Once I have all edges sorted, I pick the minimum spanning tree greedily, checking that all 6 chosen edges keep the graph connected across the 7 nodes.

Now I'm translating each tree edge into an actual corridor path on the grid, tracing rows and columns cell by cell to connect the nodes.

content.text:
I'm mapping out the graph structure, listing the nodes at their coordinates and the weighted edges connecting them across the two rows and the vertical link.

I build a minimum spanning tree from these six edges, selecting the smallest weights to connect all seven nodes while linking the left and right groups together.

Then I translate each MST edge into an actual corridor by defining the row and column ranges it spans, marking specific widths (like 9, 5, or 9 again) for each section between columns 0 and 17.
